questions.question: What entities exist, what layers constitute the system, and where can interactions occur?
questions.objective: Define the coupled Power–Transportation system boundary, entities, layers, locations, interfaces, states and service requirements, with Information and Organization as supporting domains.

questions.question: Why and through which mechanisms do components and layers affect each other?
questions.objective: Establish evidence-supported directional causal mechanisms, activation conditions, parameters, uncertainties and validity boundaries linking components and layers.

questions.question: How, when, and where do accepted interdependency mechanisms evolve and propagate through the coupled system?
questions.objective: Develop and verify a physics-based hybrid multiscale dynamic model and test its incremental explanatory or predictive value against independent and static-coupling representations.

questions.question: How is the system observed, interpreted, coordinated and controlled?
questions.objective: Evaluate how observation, state estimation, information availability, organizational constraints and feasible control affect response timing, service trajectories and recovery.

questions.question: Under what conditions can critical coupled services remain acceptable or recover under feasible controls and uncertainty, and what additional engineering information do viability and reachability provide?
questions.objective: Determine uncertainty-aware service viability and recovery reachability, evaluate incremental value beyond conventional performance/recovery curves, and characterize interface criticality as a supporting diagnostic.

questions.question: What sustainability requirements follow from resilience diagnosis and from the effectiveness, resource efficiency, and sustainability consequences of candidate interventions?
questions.objective: Derive evidence-qualified sustainability requirements from resilience diagnosis and intervention consequences, distinguishing effectiveness, resource efficiency, accessibility, energy, carbon and cost within declared accounting boundaries.

questions.question: What should be changed, where, when and in what sequence to achieve effective, efficient and sustainable infrastructure transformation under feasibility constraints and uncertainty?
questions.objective: Evaluate candidate infrastructure transformations and, where justified, intervention sequences using effectiveness, efficiency, sustainability, feasibility and uncertainty to support engineering decisions.
